previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, multiple stents, antiphospholipid syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with exertional substernal chest pain that was worse than usual. He had no EKG changes or elevated troponins, but due to his high-risk history, he was admitted for observation and treated with IV nitroglycerin and heparin. His chest pain resolved and did not recur. An exercise stress test showed no ischemic changes, supporting stable angina. He was started on isosorbide mononitrate (Imdur) for angina prophylaxis. Aspirin was discontinued due to triple antithrombotic therapy and a history concerning for prior gastrointestinal bleeding. His abdominal pain, which was unrelated to cardiac issues, will continue to be evaluated as an outpatient with a scheduled CT scan. He remained stable, was discharged home on optimized medical therapy, and advised to follow up with cardiology and primary care.

___ with PMHx extensive CAD (multiple prior PCI's, stents; most

antiphospholipid syndrome (on rivaroxaban c/b PE) who presented 
with chest pain concerning for unstable angina.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
==============
# Chest pain
# Concern for unstable angina
# CAD s/p multiple stents
Presentation consistent with possible ACS given significant risk 
factors and underlying CAD w/ multiple prior PCIs. Given 
extensive disease, concern for re-stenosis. s/p aspirin 325 in 
the ED with BNP WNL. He was maintained on heparin gtt while 
awaiting nuclear stress test. Nuclear stress on ___ 
demonstrated a reversible area of ischemia involving LAD/diag 
territory. The patient underwent coronary angiogram on ___ 
which showed stable coronary artery disease with no restenosis. 
Given these results, we believe that chest pain was likely 
non-cardiac, however patient does have ongoing CAD and severe 
small vessel disease in the Diagonals(LAD territory). Given 
this, decided to up-titrate anti-anginal regimen. Imdur dose was 
increased from 30mg to 60mg daily. Patient was continued on 
atorvastatin 80mg daily, metoprolol succ 150mg daily. Losartan 
100mg daily was held on discharge to be resumed at follow up 
pending blood pressure measurement (slightly soft BPs while 
inpatient). He was continued on clopidogrel and restarted on 
rivaroxaban following cath. ASA 81mg continued to be held.

# HFpEF (EF 60%): 
TTE from ___ with preserved EF, re-demonstrated on our 
echocardiogram ___. On Lasix 40mg PRN at home for weight 
gain. He appeared slightly volume up on admission, and so was 
diuresed once with 20 IV furosemide. He was subsequently more 
euvolemic and kept on his home PO furosemide.

owing to soft BP's, to be restarted pending blood pressure 
control as outpatient.

Held home Xarelto in setting of possible intervention, 
maintained on heparin gtt while off. Restarted xarelto on 
discharge. Continued on clopidogrel.
